clips.send: A guy stuck in a mediocre friend group sends this to himself as permission to measure his circle by results, not talk - the sting of realizing nobody around him has receipts.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says most people get the advice right - surround yourself with winners - and still get it wrong, because they can't tell a real winner from someone who just talks like one.

His fix: measure, don't listen. Arnold Schwarzenegger trained with whoever held the title, not whoever talked the biggest game. When he moved into real estate, he found out who owned the most property in Beverly Hills, then joined that man's country club.

Who are the five people you spend the most time with, and what do they actually have to show for it?

clips.send: Someone watching a friend quit on a slow-building goal sends this as a nudge - the sting of 'three years pass either way' landing on someone stalling out.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says the Greek immigrant family he worked for as a young man never had a backup plan - just a willingness to wait.

They came to America with nothing, slept in the back of the restaurant they worked in seven days a week, saved enough to bring the rest of the family over, then saved enough to buy that restaurant.

Kevin Trudeau's point: you plant a seed for an apple tree and you don't get a harvest for ten years. Most people want it the same week they plant it, and quit when it doesn't show up fast enough.

What have you quit on too early because the harvest didn't come fast enough?
